classification.difficultyReason: Read several graph intervals, compute signed gradients and distinguish speed from direction, then derive affine equations with domains and extrapolate the final return. Linked familiar rate and intercept representations, with explicit stage prompts and no new proof search.

content.prompt: The line graphs below show the journeys of Lancelot and Guinevere along a road leading out of Camelot. The vertical axis shows the distance from Camelot and the horizontal axis is the time taken after Lancelot leaves Camelot. Solid: Lancelot; dashed: Guinevere.

spec.description: All exact original marked coordinates O0/0,A20/20,B48/30,C60/18,E20/0,F60/40,2-unit grid and10-unit numbered axes. Shared curve identities retained as editable solid/dashed key.
spec.mathematics: Lancelot O-A-B-C;Guinevere E-F; all actual source values unchanged.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied journey graph only; no derived gradients/equations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the gradient of each line interval.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Give the speed of Lancelot for the different stages of his journey.

answer.worked: Speed is the magnitude of the distance-time gradient. OA gives 1, AB gives 5/14 and BC gives 1 km/min; the negative BCgradient indicates travel towards Camelot, not negative speed.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the equation of each stage of Lancelot’s journey.

answer.worked: OA passes through the origin with gradient 1: $d=t$. AB has slope 5/14 and passes through(20,20), so its intercept is $20-(\frac{5}{14})20=\frac{90}{7}$. BC has slope-1 and passes through(48,30), so $30=-48+c$ gives c=78.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the equation of Guinevere’s journey.

answer.worked: Guinevere has gradient 1 and starts at(20,0). Thus $0=20+c$, so $c=-20$ and $d=t-20$.

children.label: e
children.prompt: If Lancelot continues back to Camelot at the same speed when will he be back in Camelot?

answer.worked: Continue the final rule $d=-t+78$. At Camelot d=0, so $0=-t+78$ gives t=78 minutes after departure.
